summary: Rear range light of 1893-94 on Snug Island, Georgian Bay, at the entrance to Snug Harbour and the Parry Sound approach; a heritage lighthouse owned by Carling Township.

access.note: Reached by boat. The grounds and tower are closed.

events.note: Front and rear range lights placed in operation 29 September 1894.
Charles L. White first keeper of the Snug Harbour range.
Range buildings painted white throughout so they would show against dark shoreline.
Front light changed from fixed red to fixed white (June 1915); rear light got a new apparatus in August 1915.
Range lights changed to their present fixed green characteristic.
Live-in keeper ended in 1977 (township). The association says the keeper stayed until the mid-1970s.
Designated a heritage site by the Government of Canada.
Township says ownership passed to Carling Township the year after designation. The association says Carling decided to assume ownership in 2016.

corrections.why: The township says it took possession of the lighthouse; the association says Carling assumed ownership in 2016. LighthouseFriends still says the Canadian Coast Guard owns it. Human check needed, since the township page says the Province gave ownership (probably a slip for the federal government).
The record's point is about 0.9 km west of the rear light's position as LighthouseFriends gives it, and the record's own conflicts list gives the OSM node at 45.37379, -80.31138.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The township says the construction took place in 1893 and the building was operational the next year. LighthouseFriends says the contract was carried out in the 1893 season, the rear light was erected in 1894, and the lights were placed in operation on 29 September 1894. The association says the lighthouse 'was built in 1894'. The building year is disputed (1893 township; 1894 LighthouseFriends and association), so the record's 1893 built is kept as the township's date and is not settled. The record's 1894 first_lit matches the operating date.

notes_for_editor: OCR table matches checked on the page image (archive identifier 1910v44i11p21_0659, scan p.178, printed p.171): Adam Brown's 'April 11, 1900' appointment is on the Snug Harbour line; Red Rock is listed as '(see Snug Harbour)'; William Hughes is at Red River Range, not Red Rock. The OCR had run the Red Rock and Red River Range lines together, and the first draft misread them as Hughes at Red Rock. The 1910 statement's footnote reads '$2.00 per day for this and Snug Harbour Light', which fits one keeper at both lights. The 1906 keeper list entry for Richmond (identifier 19061907v41i9p21_0419) was matched by line; its printed page is confirmed as 165 by the corpus grep. Brown's dates conflict across sources: LighthouseFriends says a 1908 start, as Red Rock's keeper also listed at Snug Harbour; the 1910 statement gives an 1900 appointment at Snug Harbour with Red Rock under the same keeper. The 1900 date does not fit the White (1894-1902) and Richmond (1902-1907) years for Snug Harbour, so it is reported as a conflict, not resolved. Ownership conflicts: LighthouseFriends says the Canadian Coast Guard owns it; the township and the association say Carling owns it (2016 decision per association; 2017 transfer per township, which also says 'Province'). Parks Canada's Directory of Federal Heritage Designations (id 15092) could not be cited: fetch_text.to_text drops the page body, which sits inside a <form> element, so check_quotes cannot verify it. Its facts (construction 1893, established 1894, a boathouse and generator building of 1920, designation date 2016-06-14) are not used here and should be checked by hand after the extraction bug is fixed. The 1891 Boulton survey is quoted only through LighthouseFriends (not in the corpus). LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: facts are paraphrased and only short quotes are used. The 1902 painting passage is OCR'd with 'hich' for 'which' and an OCR mark before it; the story quotes only 'to render them more conspicuous against the backgrounds' and paraphrases the rest. The association also gives 1894 for the building (story says the two accounts differ) and says a keeper stayed until the mid-1970s, against the township's 1977. The association's 'shuttered ... with plywood panels' line is cited as the source of the window repainting. The focal heights differ by light (LighthouseFriends table: front 11.8 m, rear 17.5 m); the record's light block seems to take the front light's values. Not checked: parrysound.com's article on the township's overhaul (returned HTTP 429). The corpus also holds other 'Snug Harbour' entries, in British Columbia; they are a different place and are excluded. The township's 'Province' wording looks like an error.
